text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN

- The Indian military recently moved medium-range ballistic missiles to a prospective launch site near the Pakistan border, raising fresh concerns in Washington that the two enemies may have entered a provocative phase in their long-standing arms race, U.S. officials said.
- Pakistan expressed "serious concern" at India's deployment of Prithvi missiles near its border.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif called for the revival of sick industrial units as part of efforts to revive the economy.
- At least four public universities in Sindh province will soon reduce the number of departments for financial reasons.
- Commerce Minister Ishaq Dar ruled out any shortfall of sugar, saying stocks were sufficient at 2.9 million tonnes.
- Pakistan's short-term foreign debt has reached $11.11 billion, according to a State (central) Bank of Pakistan report on the economy that has been sent to parliament.
- The water and power ministry proposed withdrawing a letter of support to Gordon Wu's Consolidated Electric Power Asia for a coal-fired power plant at Keti Bander in Sindh province.
BUSINESS RECODER
- The Privatisation Commission has fixed June 12 as the bidding date for Habib Credit and Exchange Bank, which is likely to fetch $50 million, said an official.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif blamed the financial crunch faced by the electricity utilities WAPDA and KESC on the previous government's "wrong policies" on power generation.
- The National Investment Trust is to be denationalised by the Privatisation Commission.
THE NEWS
- The Foreign Office advised the Iranian emabssy to adopt security measures during the movement of embassy staff.
THE FRONTIER POST
- Former premier Benazir Bhutto said the accountability bill was aimed at whitening the black money she said had been looted by Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's family from 1985 to 1990.
THE NATION
- Benazir Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party will challenge the accountability law in the Supreme Court.
-- Islamabad newsroom 274757
